title: t-SNE
tagline: A dimensionality reduction technique built purely to make high-dimensional data visually intuitive.
what_it_is: t-SNE (t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding) is a technique that reduces high-dimensional data down to 2 or 3 dimensions for visualization, specifically preserving how close points are to their neighbors rather than the global structure of the data.
key_points: Built specifically for visualization, not general-purpose dimensionality reduction for modeling.
Focuses on preserving local neighborhood structure — points that were close in high-dimensional space stay close in the 2D/3D plot.
Does not preserve global distances well — the distance between distant clusters in a t-SNE plot is not meaningful.
Has a key hyperparameter called perplexity, which roughly controls how many neighbors it balances local vs global structure against.
Results can vary between runs and are highly sensitive to perplexity — always visualize with multiple settings.
why_it_exists: PCA preserves overall variance but can fail to reveal cluster structure that only shows up in local neighborhoods, especially for non-linear data. t-SNE exists specifically to make clusters and neighborhood relationships in high-dimensional data — like word embeddings or image features — visually obvious in a 2D plot.
intuition: Imagine trying to lay out a crumpled 3D friendship map flat on a table, where you only care about keeping close friends near each other — you're allowed to totally distort how far apart different friend groups end up from one another. t-SNE does exactly this: it obsesses over preserving 'who's near whom' locally and doesn't care about preserving the big-picture distances between separate groups.
when_to_use: Use to visually explore whether high-dimensional data (e.g. embeddings) has natural cluster structure.
Use for qualitative exploration and communication, like visualizing how a neural network separates classes internally.
when_not_to_use: Do not use t-SNE output as input features for another model — it's designed for visualization, not for preserving usable structure downstream.
Do not interpret cluster sizes or distances between clusters in a t-SNE plot as meaningful — only local neighborhoods are preserved.
Do not run it once and trust the result — always try a few different perplexity values and random seeds.
common_mistakes: Reading too much into the distance between two separate clusters in a t-SNE plot — that distance carries no real meaning.
Using a single perplexity value and assuming the resulting plot is 'the' true structure of the data.
Running t-SNE directly on very high-dimensional raw data without a faster initial reduction step (e.g. PCA first) — it can be slow.
ds_usage: Common for visualizing high-dimensional embeddings (word2vec, image features) in 2D to visually inspect cluster separation before or after modeling.
notes: UMAP is a newer, often faster alternative to t-SNE that tends to better preserve some global structure while still excelling at local neighborhoods.
